title: Canonical coefficient tensorators agree with adjunction mates and associators
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$, a finite-field datum $D$ with characteristic different from $\ell$, and the fixed closed coefficient calculus [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. Its integral and finite tensor products are the K-flat derived tensor products; write $F_n$ for integral reduction to $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(t^{n+1})$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] and $G_{n,m}$ for quotient reduction, with their specified tensorators $\mu_n,
u_{n,m}$ in the direction $F(K\otimes M)	o FK\otimes FM$. Let $e_n:G_{n,n}\simeq1$ be the identity-restriction adjunction mate and $\alpha_{n,m}:F_nG_{n,m}\simeq F_m$ the successive-restriction adjunction mate. For all ambient derived $K,M$, tensor of $e_n^{-1}$ equals $e_n^{-1}$ on tensor followed by $
u_{n,n}$, and $G_{n,m}(\mu_n)
u_{n,m}(\alpha_{n,m}\otimes\alpha_{n,m})=\alpha_{n,m}\mu_m$. Furthermore each quotient, integral-to-finite and ordinary finite-field scalar tensorator preserves the specified three-factor associator. Ordinary scalar tensorators and completed coefficient fields are those of [def-pod-scalar-completion-tensor-comparisons] and [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The five equations are given verbatim, with every component, in the Lean statement.

proof.text: Use K-flat representatives and the normalized ordinary scalar unit. The identity restriction mate sends x tensor b to bx. The fixed tensor comparisons therefore satisfy the first square.

For consecutive coefficient maps, both scalar association maps send (x tensor b) tensor c to x tensor bc. The normalized units identify this association with the stated leftAdjointCompIso. Substitute the fixed tensorator normalizations to obtain the second square.

On three factors both paths give the same ordered tensor and coefficient product. The signed total associator intertwines the differentials. This gives each of the quotient, integral reduction and ordinary finite-extension associator squares.

Naturality and uniqueness of the K-flat localization comparisons descend these representative equations to every ambient input. Zero inputs, exponent zero, the identity quotient and ramified finite extensions require no separate flatness assumption.

theorem coefficientTensor_normalization
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p) :
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      let S := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n
      let F := coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X (Nat.le_refl n)
      let μ := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.quotientCalculus.tensor
        (Nat.le_refl n)
      let e := Adjunction.leftAdjointIdIso
        ((coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.quotientCalculus.adjunction
          (Nat.le_refl n)) (normalizedDVRResUnit l E X n)
      ∀ K M : normalizedDVRDerived l E X n,
        S.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (e.inv.app K) (e.inv.app M)) =
          e.inv.app (S.tensor.obj (K, M)) ≫ μ.hom.app (K, M)) ∧
    (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      let SA := scalarIntegralClosed l E X
      let SB := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n
      let SC := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m
      let F := coefficientFiniteDerivedExtension l E X n
      let G := coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h
      let μ := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.finiteTensor n
      let ν := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.quotientCalculus.tensor h
      let ξ := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.finiteTensor m
      let α := Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso (coefficientFiniteAdjunction l E X n)
        ((coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.quotientCalculus.adjunction h)
        (coefficientFiniteAdjunction l E X m) (normalizedDVRResCompletedComp l E X D hl h)
      ∀ K M : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X),
        G.map (μ.hom.app (K, M)) ≫ ν.hom.app (F.obj K, F.obj M) ≫
            SC.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (α.hom.app K) (α.hom.app M)) =
          α.hom.app (SA.tensor.obj (K, M)) ≫ ξ.hom.app (K, M)) ∧
    (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      let SA := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n
      let SB := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m
      let F := coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h
      let μ := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.quotientCalculus.tensor h
      ∀ K M N : normalizedDVRDerived l E X n,
    μ.hom.app (SA.tensor.obj (K, M), N) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (μ.hom.app (K, M)) (𝟙 (F.obj N))) ≫
        (SB.monoidal.associator (F.obj K) (F.obj M) (F.obj N)).hom =
      F.map (SA.monoidal.associator K M N).hom ≫
        μ.hom.app (K, SA.tensor.obj (M, N)) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (F.obj K)) (μ.hom.app (M, N)))) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      let SA := scalarIntegralClosed l E X
      let SB := finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n
      let F := coefficientFiniteDerivedExtension l E X n
      let μ := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose.finiteTensor n
      ∀ K M N : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X),
    μ.hom.app (SA.tensor.obj (K, M), N) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (μ.hom.app (K, M)) (𝟙 (F.obj N))) ≫
        (SB.monoidal.associator (F.obj K) (F.obj M) (F.obj N)).hom =
      F.map (SA.monoidal.associator K M N).hom ≫
        μ.hom.app (K, SA.tensor.obj (M, N)) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (F.obj K)) (μ.hom.app (M, N)))) ∧
    ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) L] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L]
      (ι : E →ₐ[Padic l] L),
      let SA := scalarIntegralClosed l E X
      let SB := scalarIntegralClosed l L X
      let F := integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι X
      let μ := scalarClosedTensor l E L ι X
      ∀ K M N : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X),
    μ.hom.app (SA.tensor.obj (K, M), N) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (μ.hom.app (K, M)) (𝟙 (F.obj N))) ≫
        (SB.monoidal.associator (F.obj K) (F.obj M) (F.obj N)).hom =
      F.map (SA.monoidal.associator K M N).hom ≫
        μ.hom.app (K, SA.tensor.obj (M, N)) ≫
        SB.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (F.obj K)) (μ.hom.app (M, N)))
